name: Cook County

actions.title: (City of Chicago) Chicago City Council Data Center Tax Incentive Ordinance
actions.summary: Chicago's City Council approved an ordinance extending and expanding data center tax incentives, exempting qualifying data centers from the city's 9% personal property lease transaction tax and the 5.25% use tax on electricity, aiming to attract large-scale data center investment to the city.

contextBlurb: Chicago and Cook County have positioned themselves as a top-tier data center market in the Midwest, competing with Northern Virginia and Dallas. The city has used targeted tax incentives to attract hyperscale and colocation operators, though questions about grid capacity and energy costs persist as the market grows.

name: Grundy County

actions.title: (City of Morris) Microsoft Data Center Campus Siting and Tax Incentive Agreement
actions.summary: The City of Morris and Grundy County officials approved agreements supporting Microsoft's proposed multi-billion-dollar data center campus near Morris, including tax increment financing and infrastructure commitments, as part of a broader Illinois data center boom.

contextBlurb: Grundy County's City of Morris emerged as a significant data center destination after Microsoft announced a large campus investment, drawn by available land, rail and road access, and local incentive packages. The project raised community discussions about long-term tax revenue, water infrastructure demands, and electrical grid upgrades needed to support hyperscale operations.
